title: API 653 Training in New Orleans: Tank Inspector Exam Prep
description: API 653 exam prep for New Orleans tank inspectors: St. Rose and St. James terminals, LOOP, refinery tank fields and floating roofs in heavy rain. Self-paced.
h1: API 653 Aboveground Storage Tank Inspector Exam Prep for New Orleans Terminals and Refinery Tank Fields
html:
API 653 exam prep for tank inspectors on the lower Mississippi

The river below Baton Rouge is lined with tanks. Crude gathers at St. James and at LOOP's Clovelly storage in Lafourche Parish, for-hire terminals such as IMTT's at St. Rose store chemicals, fuels and vegetable oils for many customers, and five refineries keep their own crude, intermediate and product tank fields from Garyville to Chalmette. This page is for the terminal technicians, refinery tank inspectors, NDT technicians who scan floors and shells, and engineers in the New Orleans area who are preparing for the API 653 aboveground storage tank inspector examination.

There is no Atlantis classroom in New Orleans. The API 653 course is self-paced online study with an instructor answering your questions, which you can fit around terminal shifts and refinery turnarounds. The American Petroleum Institute determines eligibility under Annex D of API 653, administers the examination in person at Prometric test centres and issues the certification; the course prepares you for the examination and does not certify anyone, and Atlantis is not an API-approved training provider.

Where the tanks are, from St. James down to Chalmette

SiteWhat the operator or a public source states
IMTT, St. Rose14.7 million barrels in 203 tanks; five deepwater ship berths and 17 barge berths; access to LOOP; chemicals, ethanol, petroleum products, renewable diesel and its feedstocks, and vegetable and tropical oils
BWC Terminals, GretnaIMTT announced the sale of this terminal to BWC Terminals in January 2023, giving its storage as about 2.3 million barrels
LOOP, ClovellySalt cavern storage at the Clovelly Dome terminal and above-ground breakout tanks at the Clovelly Tank Facility; LOOP puts its storage above eighty million barrels in all
Chalmette refineryPBF's purchase announcement described a crude and product storage facility of about 7.5 million barrels of shell capacity
St. James crude hubLarge crude tank farms run by Plains and other operators, with pipeline connections to many refineries
Port of South LouisianaMore than 40 liquid and dry bulk terminals along 54 miles of river in St. Charles, St. John the Baptist and St. James parishes

Garyville, the two Norco refineries and Meraux add tank fields of their own, sized to refineries that EIA's 2026 survey rates from 125,000 to 617,000 barrels per calendar day of crude capacity. For a candidate the mix matters: a refinery tank inspector meets crude, intermediates and sour water, a terminal inspector meets whatever a customer hired the tank for this year, and a pipeline terminal inspector works under federal breakout tank rules. The API 653 tank inspection guide covers the code's structure.

For-hire terminals: one tank, many products over its life

At a for-hire terminal a tank may hold diesel for one contract, vegetable oil for the next and a chemical after that. Every switch changes the inputs an inspector relies on. The internal corrosion rate recorded under one product says little about the next one; a lining chosen for one service may not suit another; cleaning, heating and water draw practice change; and the product's specific gravity feeds straight into the shell thickness the tank needs.

API 653 treats this formally. When a change of service is planned, its suitability-for-service section asks for an evaluation that considers, among other things, the properties of the stored product such as specific gravity, temperature and corrosivity. Its brittle fracture section adds that a move to more severe service, such as a lower operating temperature or a product with a higher specific gravity, needs its own assessment, because a heavier product raises shell stresses. Good terminal records therefore keep the product history tank by tank, with dates, so that the next inspector can tell which corrosion rate belongs to which service. API RP 652, on tank bottom linings, and API RP 575 cover the practice behind those decisions; the API 575 explainer summarises the inspection recommended practice.

Worked example: a heavier product lowers the safe fill height

API 653 gives the minimum thickness of an entire shell course as tmin = 2.6 (H − 1) D G ÷ (S E), where H is the height in feet from the bottom of the course to the maximum liquid level, D the tank diameter in feet, G the specific gravity of the product, S the allowable stress in psi and E the joint efficiency, with tmin never less than 0.1 in. Rearranged, it gives the highest liquid level a corroded course can carry: Hmax = t S E ÷ (2.6 D G) + 1.

Take a hypothetical 150 ft diameter terminal tank whose bottom course, after allowing for corrosion expected before the next inspection, will average 0.600 in. Suppose the question gives S = 24,900 psi for the bottom course (the value Table 4.1 lists for A36 plate in the lower two courses) and E = 1.0 for the tank's original vertical joints.

  • Diesel, G = 0.85. Hmax = (0.600 × 24,900 × 1.0) ÷ (2.6 × 150 × 0.85) + 1 = 14,940 ÷ 331.5 + 1 = 45.07 + 1 = 46.1 ft.
  • A vegetable oil, G = 0.92. 14,940 ÷ 358.8 + 1 = 41.64 + 1 = 42.6 ft.
  • A glycol at G = 1.11. 14,940 ÷ 432.9 + 1 = 34.51 + 1 = 35.5 ft.

The same steel that could carry 46 ft of diesel can carry only about 35 ft of the glycol, so a contract that looks routine to the commercial team is a re-evaluation for the inspector. Two follow-up checks are typical exam material: repeat the calculation for the second course and each course above it at the new liquid level, because a thinner upper course may govern; and remember the brittle fracture assessment that a higher specific gravity calls for. The API 653 shell minimum thickness explainer works further cases, including locally thinned areas.

Heavy rain, floating roofs and storm season

New Orleans averages 63.4 inches of precipitation a year on NOAA's 1991 to 2020 normals, and much of it arrives in heavy bursts. On an external floating roof, rain becomes load: the primary roof drain has to carry it away, pontoons must stay tight, and a blocked or leaking drain can leave water on the deck or let product into the drain line. After heavy rain or a named storm, inspection of floating roofs moves up the list: deck and pontoon condition, drains and their check valves, seals and shoes, the gauge and guide poles, and any sign that the roof has tilted or hung up.

API 653 gives a closed-book number worth knowing here: roof plates corroded to an average thickness of less than 0.09 in. in any 100 sq in. area, or with holes through the plate, have to be repaired or replaced. Rain, humidity and storm debris also shorten the life of coatings on shells and roofs, and wet ground at the chime keeps the bottom edge of the shell damp. The floating roof inspection guide covers the roof items in more detail.

Lower-river storage that is not API 653 work

Not every tank on this river belongs to API 653, which was written for welded or riveted, atmospheric, steel tanks built to API 650 or its predecessor, API 12C. LOOP's crude in the Clovelly salt caverns is stored underground, not in tanks. The cryogenic LNG storage at Plaquemines is designed to other standards. Pressurised spheres and bullets of LPG or butane are pressure vessels, inspected under API 510. Small shop-built tanks are often inspected to STI SP001 rather than API 653; the STI SP001 and API 653 comparison explains the split. Keep this in mind when you describe your experience on the application, because API counts experience with the equipment the code covers.

Routes into API 653 for New Orleans tank people

Annex D sets the education-and-experience combinations, counted within the last 10 years while employed by or under contract with an authorized inspection agency, which includes an owner-user inspection organisation:

  • a bachelor's degree or higher in engineering or technology, or three or more years of technical military service: one year supervising or performing inspection of aboveground storage tanks;
  • a two-year degree or certificate in engineering or technology, or two years of technical military service: two years in the design, fabrication, repair, operation or inspection of tanks, one of them in inspection;
  • a high school diploma: three years on the same terms;
  • no formal education: five or more years.

Around New Orleans the candidates are terminal maintenance and inspection staff, refinery tank-field inspectors, NDT technicians who run floor scans and shell surveys, tank construction and repair welders, and engineers. Nunez Community College in Chalmette and River Parishes Community College both teach a 60-credit process technology associate degree, and API decides whether a particular degree counts under the two-year heading. NDT technicians can build their method certifications through ASNT SNT-TC-1A NDT training in New Orleans, and welders often add AWS CWI exam prep. The API 653 certification requirements page has the full rules.

Studying API 653 from a terminal schedule

Terminal work comes in uneven blocks: a tank out of service for cleaning and inspection can absorb a fortnight, then the schedule eases. Use the self-paced course the same way. Work through API 653's own rules on shell, bottom, roof and foundation evaluation in the quiet weeks, spend real time on API 650, which the open-book half leans on heavily, and keep the welding and NDE documents for later; the API 650 and API 653 comparison shows how the two codes divide the work. When a calculation or clause stalls you, send it to the instructor and keep going.

The examination is a 7.5-hour day of 170 questions, 140 scored and 30 pretest, with 110 closed-book questions in a 2.75-hour session, a 45-minute lunch, and 60 open-book questions in a 3.75-hour session where the code PDFs are provided on the computer. A short tutorial opens the day. Book through Prometric, which lists test centres in and around New Orleans, once API has accepted you for a window; the exam schedule page holds the windows and deadlines, and the API 653 course page covers the curriculum and calculations in depth.

Sponsoring tank inspectors from a terminal or refinery

A terminal operator or refinery can sponsor several candidates together, with fees quoted on request. Each candidate applies to API individually, with their own record and employer confirmation. Terminals get the most from a group when candidates study against the site's own tank files, product histories and floor scan reports, so that the code's rules attach to tanks they know, and when the employer checks each person's experience against Annex D before anyone applies.

faq.q: Can I attend an API 653 class in person in New Orleans?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in New Orleans; the course is online and self-paced, and an instructor answers your questions as you study. You go somewhere in person only to sit the examination, at a Prometric test centre booked after API accepts your application.

faq.q: Do the breakout tanks at LOOP's Clovelly facility count as API 653 experience?
faq.a: Atmospheric steel breakout tanks built to API 650 are the kind of equipment API 653 covers, and federal pipeline rules have them inspected to API 653, so supervising or performing their inspection can count. API decides on the application, so describe the tanks, the work and your role precisely, and remember that the experience has to fall within the last 10 years.

faq.q: Does inspecting the LNG tanks at Plaquemines count toward API 653?
faq.a: Generally not. Cryogenic LNG storage is designed and inspected under other standards, and API 653 was written for atmospheric steel tanks built to API 650 and its predecessor. Experience on LNG tanks may still teach you a great deal about tank inspection, but API counts experience with the equipment the code covers.

faq.q: Our terminal at St. Rose switches tanks between products. What does API 653 expect when service changes?
faq.a: An evaluation before the change. API 653 asks you to consider the new product's specific gravity, temperature and corrosivity, among other factors, and a move to a heavier product or a colder service also needs a brittle fracture assessment. In practice that means recalculating the allowable fill height course by course and reviewing the lining, the corrosion history and the heating and water draw arrangements.

faq.q: How does specific gravity enter the API 653 shell calculation?
faq.a: As G in the minimum thickness formula, t-min = 2.6 (H − 1) D G ÷ (S E). Because G multiplies the result directly, a product 30 percent heavier needs roughly 30 percent more shell thickness at the same liquid level, or a lower maximum fill height with the steel you have. Exam questions often change G and ask for the new fill height.

faq.q: After heavy rain, which floating roof items matter most?
faq.a: Start with the primary roof drain and its check valve, because a drain that cannot carry rainwater away overloads the deck, and a leaking one can let product into the drain line. Then check pontoons for water or product, the seals and shoes, the guide and gauge poles, and the deck plate. API 653 sets a repair limit for roof plates thinned below an average of 0.09 in. over any 100 sq in.

faq.q: I studied process technology at Nunez and now work at a terminal. When can I sit API 653?
faq.a: If API accepts your degree as a two-year degree or certificate in engineering or technology, you need two years of tank experience, one of them supervising or performing inspection. If not, the high school route asks for three years. Count only experience within the last 10 years, and check the details on the API 653 certification page before applying.

faq.q: Where do New Orleans candidates sit the API 653 exam?
faq.a: At a Prometric test centre; Prometric lists centres in and around New Orleans, and you choose one when API has approved your application for a window. The exam is computer-based and in person, with no books or notes allowed, and API provides the code PDFs on screen for the open-book questions.
